doc.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Drum teacher Tony Spargo and drummer idols
summary: His first teacher was Tony Spargo of the Original Dixieland Jazz Band; his idols were Wettling, Drootin and Cliff Leeman; Bill Crow's drummer T-shirt joke.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Yeah. My drummers were — the most primitive one was my drum teacher in 1949 or ’50 I guess, Tony Spargo. He was the drummer with the Original Dixieland Jazz Band.
You took lessons from Tony Spargo?
Yup. Five dollars an hour, and he would come to my house and I had to provide tea for his wife.

And after about three or four lessons Tony said, “You can keep time, I’m not going to take your money anymore.” He said, “Just travel light, keep your ears open, and you’ll do fine.” So that was my first teacher, it wasn’t very technically advanced. But then my favorite drummers were George Wettling with Condon, Buzzy Drootin and the great Cliff Leeman. Those were my idols. Keeping time, keeping time.
Keeping time. Bill Crow, the great bass player and humorist, he used to make tee shirts that said, “So many drummers, so little time.” I’m sure you know that.
That’s a good one. He played here one year for Fallcoming.
